name: Chainlink on-chain BTC/USD oracle reference
description: Tier-1 single-venue oracle reading for the Chainlink BTC/USD EACAggregatorProxy on Ethereum mainnet, read from source chainlink.ethereum.btc-usd.rounds on the oracle lane. value is the latest accepted round's answer at the feed's eight decimals. round_id is the proxy round identity as decimal text (u80 on chain, so string on the wire); phase_id is the locally derived round_id >> 64 decomposition, carried at the source's declared u64 width, and it increments when the underlying aggregator implementation is swapped. publish_time is the round's updated_at; observation_time is the decision instant; staleness_ms = observation_time - publish_time, floored at zero; update_interval_ms is the elapsed time between this round's publish time and the previous accepted one. This feed publishes on a 0.5 percent deviation threshold OR a one-hour heartbeat, so age is expected and freshness compares against a heartbeat-derived bound rather than a market-data bound: fresh when staleness_ms is at or within staleness_threshold_ms, stale otherwise. heartbeat_seconds and deviation_threshold_bps are the declared feed parameters, published so a consumer reads freshness against the feed's own contract instead of guessing it. A round_id regression is a chain reorganisation: publication is withheld with chainlink_reorg_detected until a round above the last published one is observed, never republished in place. Reads only Chainlink and predicts nothing. Not ready until the first round is accepted. Instance-status reasons: oracle_rights_gated, chainlink_warming_up, chainlink_rpc_unavailable, chainlink_round_invalid, chainlink_reorg_detected. staleness_threshold_ms defaults to 3900000 (the one-hour heartbeat plus five minutes of publication slack), heartbeat_seconds to 3600 and deviation_threshold_bps to 50. Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even.
